status: Reported as amended, first consideration, and laid on the table in the House on 2025-12-17; never removed from the table through 2026-07-31.

status: Passed House 104-95 on 2026-03-24; referred to Senate Consumer Protection and Professional Licensure Committee 2026-03-31; no further Senate action through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Data Center Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program bill; regulates commercial data centers through PUC cost responsibility, clean firm energy requirements, contract filing, backup generation, curtailment, certification, and penalties.

status: Reported as amended, first consideration, and laid on the table in the House on 2025-10-29; never removed from the table through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Load Forecast Accountability Act; gives PUC oversight of load forecasting, confidential contracts, and annual reporting in response to PJM load growth including data centers.

status: Referred to House Finance Committee 2025-12-03; no further action through 2026-07-31.

status: Passed House 133-68 on 2026-04-13; referred to Senate Environmental Resources and Energy Committee 2026-04-23; no further Senate action through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Requires annual energy and water consumption reporting by data centers and imposes penalties.

status: Passed House 124-77 on 2026-04-13; referred to Senate Local Government Committee 2026-04-23; no further Senate action through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Directs the Center for Local Government Services to provide data center ordinance assistance and model municipal standards.

status: Referred to House Education Committee 2026-01-21; no further action through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Addresses disposition of data center property tax revenue under school district tax framework.

status: Passed House 197-5 on 2026-06-25; referred to Senate Finance Committee 2026-06-26; no further Senate action through 2026-07-31.

status: Passed House 116-84 on 2026-04-27; referred to Senate Environmental Resources and Energy Committee 2026-05-01; no further Senate action through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Amends Title 27 water resources provisions for covered data centers; requires water-use review/reporting for facilities with proposed consumptive use above 100,000 gallons per day over 30 days.

status: Passed House 171-31 on 2026-06-30; referred to Senate Finance Committee 2026-07-10; no further Senate action through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Amends Right-to-Know Law to prohibit nondisclosure agreements concerning data center construction, development, or location.

status: Referred to House Energy Committee 2026-04-09; no further action through 2026-07-31.

sponsors: Rep. Paul Friel (D), with 42 bipartisan co-sponsors
status: Passed House 201-1 on 2026-06-24; referred to Senate Local Government 2026-06-25; reported as amended and re-referred to Senate Rules and Executive Nominations 2026-06-30.
key_provisions: Amends the Municipalities Planning Code to allow a municipality to impose a 180-day pause on considering new data center development applications while it establishes or revises zoning ordinances for such facilities; applications filed during the pause are deemed received once the pause ends. Appears to be the bill introduced from the 'Proposed Zoning Consideration Period' co-sponsorship memo (#48467).

sponsors: Rep. Paul Friel; Rep. Kyle Donahue; Rep. Kyle Mullins; Rep. Chris Pielli
status: Introduced as HB2496 (Rep. Paul Friel, 42 bipartisan co-sponsors), referred to House Local Government 2026-05-08; passed House 201-1 on 2026-06-24; referred to Senate Local Government 2026-06-25; reported as amended and re-referred to Senate Rules and Executive Nominations 2026-06-30.
key_provisions: Amends the Municipalities Planning Code to let a municipality impose a 180-day pause on considering data center development applications while it establishes/revises zoning ordinances for such facilities; applications submitted during the pause are automatically deemed received once the pause expires.

status: Introduced as SB1345 (Sen. Jarrett Coleman, with Sens. Gebhard, Dush, Pennycuick, Bartolotta), referred to Senate Local Government 2026-06-04; reported as committed 10-1 on 2026-06-30 (after a floor amendment to substitute statewide-moratorium language, SB1359, failed 2-9); re-reported as amended (PN 1889) by Senate Rules and Executive Nominations 2026-07-11; second consideration in the Senate 2026-07-12.
key_provisions: Amends the Municipalities Planning Code to give a municipality the option to impose a temporary (reported as up to 18 months per news coverage) moratorium on accepting/considering new applications for high-impact data centers while it revises ordinances and develops conditional-use standards.

status: Introduced as SB1359 (Sen. Katie Muth, with Sens. Comitta, Brown, Saval), referred to Senate Local Government 2026-06-04; a floor amendment attempting to fold this statewide-moratorium language into SB1345 failed 2-9 in Senate Local Government Committee on 2026-06-30; SB1359 itself remains in committee with no other action through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Imposes a statewide moratorium on hyperscale data center development and permitting (including related power generation/transmission infrastructure per the amendment description), with enforcement provisions.

sponsors: Sen. Jarrett Coleman (R), with Sens. Gebhard, Dush, Pennycuick, Bartolotta (R)
status: Referred to Senate Local Government 2026-06-04; reported as committed 10-1 on 2026-06-30; re-reported as amended (PN 1889) by Senate Rules and Executive Nominations 2026-07-11; second consideration in the Senate 2026-07-12.
key_provisions: Amends the Municipalities Planning Code to give municipalities the option to impose a temporary moratorium (reported as up to 18 months) on accepting/considering new applications for high-impact data centers while revising ordinances and developing conditional-use standards. Bill page's own 'Memo Subject' field reads 'Empowering Municipalities to Place a Moratorium on Data Center Development,' closely matching the 'Proposed municipal moratorium' co-sponsorship memo (#48540).

sponsors: Sen. Katie Muth (D), with Sens. Comitta, Brown, Saval
party: D (prime sponsor); bipartisan co-sponsors including Sen. Rosemary Brown (R)
status: Referred to Senate Local Government Committee 2026-06-04; no committee vote yet; a copy of this bill's language offered as a floor amendment to SB1345 failed 2-9 in committee on 2026-06-30, but SB1359 itself is unaffected and remains pending.
key_provisions: Imposes a statewide moratorium on hyperscale data center development and permitting, with enforcement provisions; described in press coverage as a three-year moratorium. Appears to correspond to the 'Proposed statewide moratorium' co-sponsorship memo (#48102).

key_provisions: Creates Office of Transformation and Opportunity and AI/Data Center/Emerging Technology Regulatory Sandbox Program, including high-impact data center permits for facilities with their own power.

status: Referred to Senate Environmental Resources and Energy Committee 2025-09-05; no further action through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Creates accelerated data center siting and DEP permitting process, including candidate sites and agency coordination.

status: Referred to Senate Environmental Resources and Energy Committee 2025-11-05; not adopted/agreed to by the Senate through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Directs Joint State Government Commission, PUC, DCED, and DEP to assess and recommend a comprehensive state energy strategy, including high-energy-use sectors such as data centers.

status: Prefiled and referred to House Rules 2026-01-23; subcommittee recommended continuing to 2027 (Voice Vote) 2026-02-02; Continued to 2027 in Rules Committee (Voice Vote) 2026-02-06.
key_provisions: Proposed a temporary local approval moratorium until the earlier of fulfillment of pending data center interconnection requests or 2028-07-01.

status: Passed House 2026-01-29 (90-Y 7-N); incorporates HB511 (McAuliff) 2026-01-23; passed Senate with substitute 2026-03-11 (26-Y 14-N); conference report agreed to by House and Senate 2026-03-14; enrolled 2026-03-30; Enacted, Chapter 567, approved by Governor 2026-04-13, effective 2026-07-01.
key_provisions: Adds Va. Code section 15.2-2209.4. Requires localities to obtain a sound-profile site assessment for new high energy use facilities of 100 MW or more near homes or schools within 500 feet; allows optional review of water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forestland.

status: Prefiled 2026-01-06; referred to House Labor and Commerce; subcommittee recommended laying on the table (9-Y 0-N) 2026-02-10; Left in Labor and Commerce (and Education) 2026-02-18 - bill died in House committee.
key_provisions: Would require State Corporation Commission certificates of operation for new high-load facilities exceeding 25 MW, including review of grid sufficiency and customer cross-subsidy risks.

status: Passed House 2025-01-23 (57-Y 40-N); passed Senate with substitute 2025-02-12; conference report agreed to 2025-02-22; enrolled 2025-03-07; House rejected Governor's recommended amendments 2025-04-02 (11-Y 85-N); Vetoed by Governor 2025-05-02 (veto sustained; no override vote recorded).
key_provisions: Required a high energy use facility site assessment before rezoning, special exception, or special use permit approvals, with mandatory noise review within 500 feet and optional review of water, agriculture, parks, historic, and forest impacts.

status: Passed House 2024-02-13 (55-Y 42-N); Senate continued the bill to 2025 in General Laws and Technology (9-Y 3-N 3-A) 2024-02-28; Left in General Laws and Technology 2024-11-19 with no further floor or committee action recorded in the 2025 session - bill died at the end of the 2024-2025 House term.
key_provisions: Would allow local site assessments before data center siting approvals; House-passed version focused on water use and carbon emissions.

status: Passed House 2026-02-17 (74-Y 23-N); passed Senate with substitute 2026-03-04 (25-Y 15-N); conference report agreed to 2026-03-14; enrolled 2026-03-30; Enacted, Chapter 623, approved by Governor 2026-04-13, effective 2027-01-01.
key_provisions: Requires registered water users that provide offsite water to report potable and reclaimed water volumes supplied to data centers with DEQ air permits, along with other use categories where available.

status: Prefiled 2026-01-12; referred to House Labor and Commerce; subcommittee recommended continuing to 2027 (Voice Vote) 2026-02-10; Continued to 2027 in Labor and Commerce (Voice Vote) 2026-02-12.
key_provisions: Would prevent utility costs substantially related to serving data center customers of 100 MW or more from being recovered from non-data-center customers unless rates substantially recover those costs from data centers.

key_provisions: Related site-assessment bill incorporated into the enacted HB153 framework.

status: Prefiled 2026-01-13; referred to House Finance; Continued to 2027 in Finance (Voice Vote) 2026-02-11.

status: Prefiled 2026-01-06; reported from Senate Local Government (15-Y 0-N) 2026-01-19; Incorporated by Finance and Appropriations into SB94 (Roem) (13-Y 2-N) 2026-02-03.

status: Prefiled 2026-01-13; referred to Senate Agriculture, Conservation and Natural Resources; passed by indefinitely there 2026-01-27, then rereferred to Finance and Appropriations 2026-02-03 (14-Y 0-N); Continued to 2027 in Finance and Appropriations (15-Y 0-N) 2026-02-10.

status: Prefiled 2026-01-14; referred to Senate Agriculture, Conservation and Natural Resources; failed to report (defeated) there (7-Y 7-N) 2026-01-27, then reported and rereferred to Local Government (9-Y 5-N) same day; Failed to report from Local Government with amendments (7-Y 7-N 1-A) 2026-02-02 - bill died in committee.
